name: Cartouche
subtitle: Cartouche itself
description: The source Cartouche's built-in SideStore reads for Cartouche's own updates. It lists Cartouche and nothing else: Cartouche never lists, hosts or downloads games.

apps.name: Cartouche
apps.subtitle: Play your own games built with nxnative
apps.localizedDescription: Cartouche runs the games you build with nxnative from your own copies, renews itself without a computer, and gives them Increased Memory Limit. It never downloads a game.

versions.localizedDescription:
Games nxnative built without their game files now install with the romfs.img beside them, and Google Drive joins your storage.

- Games: an nxnative IPA built without its game files installs with the romfs.img beside it in your games folder. Cartouche checks the image against the IPA before it unpacks anything, copies it into the game and keeps it across the game's updates. The storage page says which games lack their image, instead of finding no game.
- Storage: Google Drive, through an OAuth client of the iOS type that you make in your own Google Cloud project, with a step-by-step guide: Cartouche ships no Google key. A project left in testing asks you to sign in again every 7 days, and Cartouche then offers Sign in to Google again, without an error.
- Storage: an SMB server no longer hangs up when two requests leave at once on one connection, and an install from a shared folder keeps its memory.
- Installs: an install, or a copy to your games folder, goes on after you leave Cartouche, with its progress in a Live Activity whose stop button stops it.
- Installs: an IPA from Files that is damaged or cut short is refused, with nothing installed, and Cartouche says to copy it again; so is a zip with no app in a Payload folder, and an app whose Info.plist cannot be read, instead of an app named Unknown.
- Import a game opens one Files picker over whatever is on screen, which B closes: Cartouche no longer freezes there.
- Games: a game Cartouche does not know takes its platform from its ID, and its cover and genre from IGDB. Edit the game's info changes any game's name, platform, genre, description or cover, from Photos or Files, on this iPhone only.
- Games: each game's sheet shows its description under its name, IGDB's summary or your own. On iOS 18 and later, the iPhone translates IGDB's summary into Cartouche's language itself, with Translate when the languages are not downloaded yet, and Show the original.
- Games: a game behind the console turns only as its own app allows, so a game made for landscape stays in landscape.
- Games: on an iPhone whose graphics cannot read the textures of nxnative's games, the A16's and older, an install asks first, and the game's sheet and the System page say why. When a game's process behind the console lacks Increased Memory Limit, games start in Cartouche's place.
- Apple ID: when Apple refuses more sign-ins for a while, Cartouche says so and counts the wait down before signing in again. It checks that it reaches the iPhone before anything goes to Apple, and Register this iPhone takes that step alone, by itself once LocalDevVPN connects. A sign-in that stopped before the certificate no longer reads as signed in: Cartouche says why, with Copy the report and Sign in again, and signs in again by itself once after it is installed again.
- Renewal: Cartouche renews itself alone, even when another SideStore of the same Apple ID lists other apps, and reads its expiry again when SideStore stops on the way.
- Your own certificate: the new Cartouche Installer can install Cartouche signed with your own signing certificate (.p12) and its provisioning profile, without an Apple ID, LocalDevVPN or a renewal each week. Games then start in Cartouche's place, and most of them do not start without Increased Memory Limit in the profile. The Apple ID stays the default. Thanks to javi11.
- The iPhone can lock again after a game failed to start behind the console.
- Measurements: a game's frame rate leaves out its pauses, behind the console or with Cartouche in the background; each session's memory goes with the game that ran it; turning measurements off also stops a report on its way; SideStore's errors say what is behind them.
- Mac: Cartouche Builder 0.5.0 imports an nxnative IPA with its romfs.img, builds a game from the last nxnative commit that built when the newest does not, and says why a game was not built. It updates itself to it.

Signing in with your Apple ID should go through now, as it does with the Cartouche Installer.

- Apple ID: since October, Apple refuses a sign-in that says it comes from one kind of computer while its sign-in data comes from another, and Cartouche stopped with -80045, -80046 after the code, or -45061 "reprovision required", which installing Cartouche again did not fix. Cartouche now signs in the way the Cartouche Installer does, which Apple accepts for the same accounts, and starts afresh by itself when a sign-in server or Apple refuses it.
- If Cartouche never got past its Apple ID step, it cannot update itself: install this version with the Cartouche Installer, then sign in again.
- An Apple ID signed in already keeps its current way until it signs in again, and its renewals go on as before.
- Measurements: an error with the sign-in servers counts as theirs, and an iPhone with no connection counts as offline first.

Errors now say why they happened, so that each one can be fixed sooner.

- Measurements: each error Cartouche sends says its cause, from a fixed list, the step it stopped at, how far it got and how long it took. For the Apple ID sign-in, the renewal and the update of Cartouche, which the built-in SideStore runs, it also says where SideStore stopped and Apple's code, and a sign-in that goes through says how long it took. Never an error's words, your Apple ID, a path or an address. System › Game measurements lists what is sent, with the switch that turns it off.
- Reports: Copy the report, under an error, now gives the error's cause too.
- Mac: Cartouche Builder 0.4.1's errors say where in its engine they happened, and Cartouche Builder updates itself to it.

Your saves follow you, even after Cartouche is installed again, and Your first game no longer insists on a Mac.

- Saves: each game's saves stay in step with your saves folder, both ways. Before a game starts, Cartouche takes the newest copy when the folder has one, as after another iPhone played it; after the game, the saves that changed go. When both changed, the saves written last win, and the others stay in the folder as a copy with their date.
- Saves: a game installed again, as after Cartouche itself was installed again, gets its saves back. Your servers and folders, without their passwords, are now also kept in the keychain, which iOS keeps when an app is deleted, so a new install of Cartouche finds your storage again: open this version once before you uninstall Cartouche.
- Games: a game's sheet shows what came and what was kept, the last sync, and Sync with … now.
- Memory: with Game Mode, Cartouche has about 8 GiB on a 12 GB iPhone, and a game behind the console about 6 GiB. A game that needs more than it has behind the console starts in Cartouche's place; the others wait behind the console. A game's sheet compares its peak with the most memory Play can give it.
- Setup: in Your first game, No thanks skips the Mac's step, for games built already or without a Mac. The home's card has a × that takes it away, and System › Your first game opens the guide again. Send the steps to my Mac sends Cartouche Builder's page.
- iPhone Duo: unfolded, before your first game, the console takes the whole display, and a game's sheet moves beside it once you have one. All games' filters scroll from edge to edge.
- Mac: Cartouche Builder 0.3.0 opens a setup assistant at its first start, and 0.2.0 updates itself to it.

A game waits behind the console, your Mac can be your storage, and a guide takes you to your first game.

- Games: the Home button, on screen or on a controller, brings the console back without ending the game, which waits behind it, paused. Resume goes back to it, Quit ends it. A game that needs more memory than it gets there starts in Cartouche's place, as before.
- Games: a game starts in your iPhone's language when it has it. Its settings can choose another.
- Games: Cartouche runs in iOS's Game Mode, for the most of the CPU and GPU and the lowest latency of your controllers. iOS says so when it comes on.
- Games: a game's sheet shows your play time, your sessions and when you last played, and the room the game takes on this iPhone and in your games folder. The home shows them under the game in focus.
- Home: your games alone, on one shelf, with larger covers. Shorter texts everywhere, and dark System pages. On an unfolded iPhone Duo, the home and the sheet of the game in focus stand on either side of the fold.
- Storage: System › Storage › Add your Mac (Cartouche Builder) pairs Cartouche with Cartouche Builder on your Mac, once, with the same six digits on both screens. Your games then install from the Mac and your saves go to it, encrypted on the way.
- Storage: away from home or off your VPN, a server that does not answer shows as offline within seconds, with no error, and your saves wait until it answers again. An install that the network cuts off for a moment picks up where it stopped.
- Errors: under each error, Copy the report gives what it takes to understand it, never a password or an address. System › Report a problem shows a report in full and sends nothing until you choose how: Send to Cartouche, share it, copy it, or open it on GitHub.
- Setup: on a new install, Your first game takes you from LocalDevVPN to your first game and ticks each step by itself. It stays at the top of the home until a game is installed.
- Catalog: All games lists the games nxnative added since 0.9.0 and marks the 64 it plays on the iPhone. New games get their covers within a day, without a new version of Cartouche.
- Game measurements: after each game session, Cartouche sends what nxnative measured, such as the frame rate and the memory, with its own events, and never your files, saves, accounts or the addresses of your storage. It does so unless you turn it off in System › Game measurements, which also shows the last report and erases what this iPhone sent. All that is sent: https://github.com/clabeuhtegrite/Cartouche/blob/main/docs/privacy.md

Cartouche offers to update a game when your games folder holds a newer build of it.

- Games: when your games folder holds a newer IPA of a game you installed, a later version of the game, or the same version built again from a newer nxnative, such as one Cartouche Builder made, the console shows Update for the game and a badge on its cartridge, and its sheet Update from your games folder. The game's settings and saves stay.
- Games: a game's sheet shows which build of it is on this iPhone, and the newer one in your games folder: its version, the nxnative commit it was built from and when it was built.
- Games: a copy Cartouche writes of a game to your games folder keeps when the game was built, so that it is never offered as an update over the same game.

Games install from your storage again, and the icon keeps no badge.

- Install: a game whose IPA holds a large deflated file, such as a RomFS image of several GB, installs from your shared folder, S3 bucket or server. Cartouche stopped with "romfs.img is damaged (its deflated data ends early)": the end of the file was never decoded.
- Icon: Cartouche's icon no longer shows a badge with nothing behind it. The built-in SideStore counted the available updates there and never took the count away; Cartouche clears it when it opens.

Your games and saves on an SFTP server of yours.

- Storage: System › Storage › Add an SFTP server reaches a server of yours, such as your NAS's or your Mac's, with your account on it. Your games folder and saves folder can be there, as on a shared folder.
- Storage: Cartouche keeps the server's key when you save it and shows its fingerprint. Should the server show another key later, Cartouche stops before sending your password; if you reinstalled the server, remove it in Cartouche and add it again. Your password stays in this iPhone's keychain.

Your games and saves on an FTP server of yours.

- Storage: System › Storage › Add an FTP server reaches a server of your network, such as your NAS's, with your account on it. Your games folder and saves folder can be there, as on a shared folder.
- Storage: FTP sends your password unencrypted, so use it on your own network. Cartouche keeps the password in this iPhone's keychain.

Your games and saves on an S3 bucket of yours.

- Storage: System › Storage › Add S3 storage reaches a private bucket on Amazon S3, or on a server of your own such as MinIO on your NAS, with your access key. Your games folder and saves folder can be there, as on a shared folder.
- Storage: every request is signed with your keys, and the secret key stays in this iPhone's keychain. Cartouche reaches no public bucket.
- Storage: type http:// before the address of a server on your network without HTTPS; Cartouche uses HTTPS otherwise.
